A weeknight pasta with lemon and peas

By Test Author · 4 November 2026

This is a simple pasta for evenings when you have twenty minutes and not much in the fridge. It uses frozen peas, a lemon, parmesan and whatever short pasta you have.

Bring a large pan of salted water to the boil and cook the pasta according to the packet. Two minutes before it is done, add the peas. Meanwhile, zest and juice the lemon.

Drain the pasta and peas, keeping a cup of the cooking water. Return everything to the pan with the butter, lemon zest, half the juice and most of the parmesan. Add cooking water a splash at a time until the sauce coats the pasta.

Season generously with black pepper. Taste and add more lemon if it needs lifting. Serve with the remaining cheese.

A note on peas: frozen peas are picked and frozen within hours and are often sweeter than fresh ones sold days later, according to this guide. Fresh peas in season are lovely but not necessary here.

Serves two. Leftovers keep for a day in the fridge and reheat well with a splash of water.
